  Commissioners Present: Bedy, Chotiswatdi, Killion, Noble, Russell, Scott, Wood

  Commissioners Absent: Hilliard, Howat, Lie

Also present: Paul Duncan, Homeless Services Bureau Manager, Joseph Botelho, Community
Program Specialist V, Jennifer Santana, Community Program Specialist.

Roll call taken by Jennifer Santana.
  • For the record commissioner Angela Russel joined the meeting at 4:03 p.m.and commissioner
  Sarah Bedy stepped out of the meeting for 50 minutes.

REGULAR AGENDA

1.  26-54676  Recommendation to approve the minutes for the Homeless Services Advisory

  A motion was made by Member Bedy, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Wood, Scott, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Lie, Russell, Howat, Hilliard

2.  26-54677  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation from the Ethics Department

  and the City Attorney’s Office on the 2026 Annual Ethics Update, including the
  Brown Act and Robert’s Rules of Order.

  A motion was made by Member Noble, seconded by Member Killion, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Lie, Howat, Hilliard, Bedy

  • City staff member Heather Van Wijk from the Office of Ethics and
  Transparency provided an annual ethics refresher presentation.The
  presentation included the Office of Ethics and Transparency (OET) mission,
  accomplishments, framework for ethical decision-making, and what is
  coming in 2026, including the FAIR Act, which is currently under review by
  the City Council.
  • Heather reviewed the advisory body’s role and influence in decision-making.
  Annual reports are used to reflect the work and priorities of the commission.
  She provided guidance on how meetings should be conducted, including
  unbiased decision-making, required commissioner trainings, and information
  on the Ethics Helpline and other resources available for staff and
  commissioners.
  • City Attorney Nicholas Masero provided an overview of the Brown Act and
  Robert’s Rules. Key points discussed included understanding why we follow
  the Brown Act and Robert’s Rules, agenda and posting requirements, public
  rights, and violations and penalties.
  • Government decisions must be made openly so the public can observe,
  participate, and hold officials accountable.
  • The meeting was adjourned for two minutes while quorum was regained.
  Serial communications and examples of prohibited communications were
  discussed.
  • Violations of the Brown Act can result in civil lawsuits or criminal
  penalties.Robert’s Rules help conduct meetings in an orderly and efficient
  manner.
  • Member Noble commented on the lack of discussion time during meetings
  for both commissioners and public comment. She also requested clarification
  on prohibited communication between commissioners. City Attorney
  Nicholas Masero provided feedback.

3.  26-57043  Recommendation to receive and file updates from the Mayor’s Fund and Policy
  Subcommittee and the Continuum of Care (CoC) Homeless Services Advisory
  Committee (HSAC) representative.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Lie, Howat, Hilliard

  Policy Subcommittee Updates
  • Member Sarah Bedy provided an update from the last subcommittee
  meeting. The subcommittee is working on the Annual Report and Policy
  recommendations for this upcoming year. A draft was presented to the
  committee, the subcommittee would like to receive feedback from the
  committee regarding the drafted recommendations. They will work on the
  final draft and discuss at the next subcommittee meeting in May.
  • Member Chotiswatdi provided feedback and suggestions for future
  recommendation.
  Mayor’s Fund Subcommittee
  • The subcommittee will meet on April 13, 2026, no meeting was held in March
  due to quorum issues.
  • The Mayor’s Fund balance sheet for November and December 2025 was
  provided, these two months reflect an increase in donations.
  CoC Updates
  • Member Scott provided a brief update, noting a lack of funding and that no
  new projects will be started due to the funding loss.
  • Health Department staff member Joseph Botelho provided a brief update on
  the preliminary injunctions related to the 2025 Notice of Funding Opportunity
  (NOFO) that HUD had attempted to release. The court has determined,
  through a preliminary injunction, that HUD is not able to move forward. The
  Consolidated Appropriations Act states that HUD must release the 2026
  NOFO by June 1.
  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan added a comment regarding HUD executing
  2025 contracts for the bureau. The bureau can now draw down funds and
  begin making payments.

5.  26-54679  Recommendation to receive and file a presentation on updates for the City of Long
  Beach Rent assistance program and the 582 Emergency Housing Vouchers from
  the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Noble, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  6  Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 4  Lie, Howat, Hilliard, Bedy

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided an update on the 582 Emergency
  Housing Vouchers launched under the American Rescue Plan Act in 2021.
  This was designed to support the housing stability during COVID-19 and was
  expected to run through 2030.
  • The Housing Authority of the City of Long Beach currently assists 500
  households, all households and landlords were notified as of March 19, 2026
  that these vouchers are expected to end in October 2026.
  • A 60 day notice before final payment will be issued to both landlords and
  households.
  • All EHV households have been added to Housing Choice Voucher waitlist
  via an approved HUD waiver.
  • Unfortunately, the Hosuing Authority does not currently have any other
  funding to shift these vouchers and the City and Staff continue to advocate
  and look for other funding sources.
  • There is some potential for 125 transitional vouchers from the HUD budget

  but that would not be enough to sustain the 500 families that are being
  affected.
  • At this moment there is no clear answer on how this situation will be
  resolved, but staff will continue to advocate at a federal and state level.
  • Member questions included options for shared housing, what type on lease
  are these households currently on, and what kind of protection is available to
  them during this time. There is also a request for the demographics of the
  makeup of the landlords that currently participate in this program. Are there
  other options that can be explored for inclusionary housing.
  • Members would like to get a 6 month update regarding the housing
  vouchers.
  • A member of the public provided a comment regarding inflated rent and why
  funding is running out. The Mayor stated the 2026 budget plan would
  allocate money to homelessness prevention , is any of that going to be used
  to help keep households housed?

6.  26-54680  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Quarterly
  Operations Data Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Lie, Howat, Hilliard

  • Health Department staff member Dalton Dorr provided a quarterly data
  report demonstrating the flow of individuals entering and exiting the system.
  • New enrollments across site-based programs and the Mobile Access Center
  remain fairly stable, with trends aligning with expected seasonal patterns.
  Typically, enrollments increase during the summer months and decrease
  during the winter months.
  • Permanent supportive housing has the least amount of movement compared
  to other programs, a spike in PH is generally due to a new project opening.
  • Exits to permanent housing was discussed, there is a steep decline of exits,
  that is partially due to errors in the system that have now been fixed however
  the data is still represented on the graph.
  • Members of the committee engaged in conversation regarding the data that
  was presented.
  • A member of the public had a question regarding supportive housing.

7.  26-54678  Recommendation to receive and file the Homeless Services Bureau Staff

  Operations and Updates Report from the Health Department.

  A motion was made by Member Killion, seconded by Member Chotiswatdi, to
  approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  7  Wood, Scott, Russell, Noble, Killion, Chotiswatdi, Bedy
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 3  Lie, Howat, Hilliard

  • Bureau Manager Paul Duncan provided staffing updates, a budget picture of
  the fiscal year 2026/2027 remains uncertain. There are funding sources that
  will have reductions.
  • The city budget is about to kick-off with each department submitting a
  department budget for consideration. Long Beach will be required to
  prioritize and allocate funding that is received.
  • The county is facing a $200 million projected budget deficit going into next
  year.
  • Looking into the next 2 to 3 years, there could be significant challenges and
  reductions. There is roughly a 25% reduction in county measure funding that
  comes into homelessness and homeless prevention.
  • Encampment resolution finalized lease with colonial motel on 3/17/26
  focused on homelessness around the riverbed.
  • The City has made the decision to end its contract with First to Serve Inc.
  effective 3/31/2026. The City has executed a single year contract, with one
  three month extension option, with People Assisting the Homeless (PATH) to
  assume operations for the four City owned and funded shelters.
  • A member of the public provided a public comment.
